title: Introduce two-step operator approvals and KMS callproofs with audit watermarking
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds operator two-step approval flow, KMS callproof header for non-repudiation, and server-side audit watermarking. No customer-facing API changes. Backwards compatible with RBAC v2 rollout.
description: Summary: Implement a two-step operator approval queue for high-risk operator actions (region pin changes, KMS key rebinds, operator impersonation). Add a KMS callproof header (X-KMS-CallProof) signed by the service HSM to make KMS usage non-repudiable when bridging tenant scopes. Persist an audit watermark per-tenant to deterministically order edge-forwarded audit batches. Motivation: several incidents highlighted gaps where operator actions could be executed by a single privileged session and telemetry could not deterministically order cross-region audit records. This PR reduces blast radius and provides cryptographic proof of KMS delegations for compliance reviews.
detailed_description:
Design highlights and rationale: - Operator approvals: New DB table operator_approvals (id, requester_id, action, target, status, approver_id, expires_at, created_at). Actions flagged as high-risk are routed to the approval queue via operator-gateway middleware. Approvals require a second distinct operator principal and are enforced in RBAC v2 policy checks.
- KMS callproofs: When an internal KMS proxy performs tenant-key operations across zone boundaries, it now attaches X-KMS-CallProof containing a base64(serialized_proof). The proof is an HMAC-SHA256 over (request_id | tenant_id | kms_operation | timestamp) using the service HSM signing key. The runtime validates callproofs for replay and provenance in the audit-processor.
- Audit watermarking: Each tenant audit-forwarder now keeps a monotonic watermark value (tenant_audit_watermark) that increments for each forwarded batch. The watermark is stored in the tenancy metadata store to maintain ordering across distributed forwarders. This enables deterministic replay and simplifies compliance exports. Backwards compat: middleware tolerates absent callproof headers; audit-processor tags such records as legacy and applies stricter sampling for lineage reconstruction.
Security considerations: ties approvals to operator session id and requires operator role separation. Proof signatures are rotated via existing KMS key rotation tooling.
Testing notes: unit tests cover approval enqueue/dequeue, signature verification, and watermark increments. Integration harness simulates cross-zone replay and validates no ordering regressions.

Security scan: verified no leakage of raw keys; callproofs are HMAC-only and not reversible.
